front: Rule 1. The slip: the used deer tag stays home on the fridge. What is the rule?
back: Every species licence bought this licence year rides with you while you hunt, cancelled or not (99%). Fix: one wallet pocket holds every tag until 31 March.

front: Rule 2. The slip: "It is all on their app", so no ID in the pocket. What is the rule?
back: You must know or produce your FWID (Fish and Wildlife ID) number and photo ID when an officer asks (99%). Fix: photo ID in the wallet, FWID number memorized.

front: Rule 3. The slip: buying the deer tag online the night before opening day. What is the rule?
back: A species licence bought online is mailed; in person you get it at once (99%). You must carry it to hunt (99%). Fix: buy in person, or online weeks ahead.

front: Rule 4. The slip: buying a cougar or bobcat licence on the day you hunt. What is the rule?
back: Cougar, goat, sheep, caribou, bobcat, lynx and wolverine licences are not valid until 2 days after issue (99%). Fix: buy it at least 2 days early. Deer, moose, elk and bear have no wait (99%).

front: Rule 5. The slip: winning the draw and thinking that is all. What is the rule?
back: An LEH (Limited Entry Hunting) authorization is not a licence. You still need the hunting licence and the species licence (99%). Fix: draw, hunting licence, species licence: all three.

front: Rule 6. The slip: your brother tags the deer you shot because he still has a tag. What is the rule?
back: Never use another person's licence, and never lend or transfer yours, for any reason (99%). Fix: the hunter who kills it cancels their own licence.

front: Rule 7. The slip: "I have my BC licence." What is the rule?
back: For ducks, geese, coots, snipe, doves and band tailed pigeons, carry the federal MGBHP (Migratory Game Bird Hunting Permit) with its stamp, plus your BC licence (99%). Fix: buy the federal permit before the first duck hunt.

front: Rule 8. The slip: hunting spring bear in April on last fall's licence. What is the rule?
back: All hunting and species licences expire 31 March. The licence year runs 1 April to 31 March (99%). Fix: buy the new year's licence before any April hunt.

front: Rule 9. The slip: hunting Mission ducks on only the regular licence. What is the rule?
back: All of MU (Management Unit) 2-4, and 2-8 inside Mission, Maple Ridge, Pitt Meadows and Coquitlam, need the Fraser Valley Special Area licence plus $1,000,000 liability insurance (99%). Fix: buy the $10 special licence and carry the insurance.

front: Rule 10. The slip: "I lost last month's used deer tag, it does not matter now." What is the rule?
back: A lost, stolen or destroyed species licence, cancelled or not, must be replaced if you keep hunting this licence year (99%). Fix: FrontCounter BC or Service BC, $10, declare the harvest if it was cancelled (99%).

front: Rule 11. The slip: thinking CORE (Conservation and Outdoor Recreation Education) plus a hunting licence covers the rifle. What is the rule?
back: A BC hunting licence gives no authority to carry a firearm (99%). Fix: hold the federal firearms licence too, the PAL (Possession and Acquisition Licence) (95%).

front: Rule 12. The slip: "Chamber is empty, so it is unloaded." What is the rule?
back: Rounds in the chamber, a fixed magazine, a hinged floor plate, or a detachable magazine clipped in: any one means Loaded (99%). Fix: magazine out, chamber empty, then look again.

front: Rule 13. The slip: riding the quad with the magazine still clipped in. What is the rule?
back: No live round in the chamber or attached magazine in or on a truck, ATV (All Terrain Vehicle), bicycle, sleigh or other conveyance (99%). Fix: unload fully before you climb on anything with wheels.

front: Rule 14. The slip: loading up while idling to the decoys. What is the rule?
back: Since 1 October 2026 a loaded firearm in or on a boat is banned. The exemption covers hunting from a boat with no motor, or one its motor is not propelling (99%). Fix: load only with the motor off. Your kayak, with no motor, fits the exemption (95%).

front: Rule 15. The slip: pulling the plug for grouse or quail. What is the rule?
back: To hunt with a pump or semi auto shotgun, the magazine needs a plug so it holds no more than 2 shells (99%). Fix: plug in all season. Only slugs for big game may skip it (99%).

front: Rule 16. The slip: range ammo in the Tikka on a deer trip. What is the rule?
back: No hunting with full metal jacket non expanding bullets, or tracer, incendiary or explosive bullets (99%). Fix: hunting bullets only in the hunting pack. Range boxes stay home.

front: Rule 17. The slip: a handgun on the belt to finish a wounded animal. What is the rule?
back: No hunting with a handgun, and no long gun with a barrel under 305 mm (12 in) (99%). Fix: finish it with your legal rifle or shotgun.

front: Rule 18. The slip: a grouse load in the 12 gauge when a deer steps out. What is the rule?
back: For deer, a 20 gauge or larger with No. 1 Buck or larger shot, or slugs (99%). Fix: no buckshot or slug in the pocket, no deer shot.

front: Rule 19. The slip: the CZ .22 on an Okanagan quail covey. What is the rule?
back: A rimfire is legal for grouse, ptarmigan and turkey only among birds, and never for deer. A centrefire is legal for grouse and ptarmigan only (99%). Fix: quail, chukar, pheasant, partridge: shotgun, air gun or bow.

front: Rule 20. The slip: an uncased rifle on the back seat through a park. What is the rule?
back: No hunting in any National Park. Passing through, the firearm is dismantled, cased, or wrapped and tied, and it stays in the vehicle (99%). Fix: case it before the park gate.

front: Rule 21. The slip: resting the rifle on the open truck window, engine off. What is the rule?
back: No hunting wildlife from a motor vehicle: truck, ATV (All Terrain Vehicle), snowmobile (99%). Fix: get out, walk off the road allowance, then hunt (rule 22).

front: Rule 22. The slip: a shot from the gravel shoulder. What is the rule?
back: No hunting or shooting within the road allowance of numbered highways and 2 lane or bigger public roads, and no shooting across them (99%). Fix: under 3 lanes, walk past 15 m (16 yd) from the middle of the road (99%).

front: Rule 23. The slip: a rifle shot 150 m off the Coquihalla. What is the rule?
back: Highway 5 from Hope to the Highway 1 junction at Kamloops: no bullet or slug within 400 m (437 yd) of either side of the road allowance (99%). Fix: walk past 400 m with the rifle. Shot for grouse is allowed in the band (99%).

front: Rule 24. The slip: "I only used the quad to drag the deer out." What is the rule?
back: In a Motor Vehicle for Hunting Closed Area, no vehicle to hunt, carry hunters, carry gear or haul game (99%). Fix: in MU (Management Unit) 3-28, 1 September to 10 December, no ATV or e bike for any hunting use (99%).

front: Rule 25. The slip: "There was no gate sign, so it was open." What is the rule?
back: A closure covers private land inside it unless exempted. If a sign and the regulation disagree, the regulation wins (99%). Fix: check the closure list for your MU before the trip.

front: Rule 26. The slip: cutting a new quad track across an alpine meadow. What is the rule?
back: In Regions 3 and 8, above 1,700 m (5,577 ft), motor vehicles stay on existing roads and trails, all year. Snowmobiles are not covered (99%). Fix: paved, logging, mining or service roads, or a bare two track only.

front: Rule 27. The slip: your brother rides the second quad with no driver's licence on him. What is the rule?
back: Riding an ATV on a Forest Service Road needs a valid driver's licence and at least $200,000 third party liability insurance (99%). Fix: both riders carry a driver's licence; insure the quads.

front: Rule 28. The slip: no plate on the quad, helmet left at camp. What is the rule?
back: ORVs (Off Road Vehicles) on Crown land must be registered with the plate or sticker shown. Helmet on any ORV you sit astride; seatbelt if fitted (99%). Fix: plate front, back or left side; helmet on every ride.

front: Rule 29. The slip: running the boat at a raft of ducks to push them to your brother. What is the rule?
back: No using a power boat, aircraft, motor vehicle or other machine to herd or harass wildlife (99%). Fix: let birds and deer move on their own.

front: Rule 30. The slip: shooting a grouse on the bank from the moving boat. What is the rule?
back: Deer, grouse and other game that is not a migratory bird: never hunt from a boat while its motor propels it (99%). Fix: motor off, or beach the boat, before any shot. Ducks: rule 70.

front: Rule 31. The slip: "The farmer said go ahead," 60 m from his house. What is the rule?
back: No hunting or shooting within 100 m (109 yd) of a dwelling, an occupied farm or ranch building, a church, a school, a playground or a regional district park (99%). Fix: pace 100 m from any occupied building before you load.

front: Rule 32. The slip: an empty lease pasture, so "no cows, no problem". What is the rule?
back: No hunting cultivated land, or a Crown grazing lease with livestock on it, without the owner's, lessee's or occupant's consent (99%). Fix: ask first. Leased land is under the Trespass Act even with no cattle (99%).

front: Rule 33. The slip: "There was only one sign, at the far gate." What is the rule?
back: Private or leased land is enclosed if it has signs at each normal way in, or a lawful fence all round, or a natural boundary all round (99%). Fix: any one of the three means ask the owner first (90%).

front: Rule 34. The slip: cutting across reserve land to reach Crown land. What is the rule?
back: Indian Reserves are private land. Get permission from the band office to hunt on them or even to cross them (99%). Fix: call the band office first, or go around.

front: Rule 35. The slip: a legal buck, legal season, on land you had no right to be on. What is the rule?
back: Killing wildlife while breaking any other law, trespass included, is its own offence (99%). Fix: know whose land you stand on before the shot.

front: Rule 36. The slip: walking a park trail with the shotgun because grouse are "always open". What is the rule?
back: Before hunting a BC Park, confirm its own page allows hunting. If closed, a firearm or bow may only be in a vehicle (99%). Fix: read the park page. No hunting within 400 m (437 yd) of a park road (99%).

front: Rule 37. The slip: a grouse shot from the campsite picnic table. What is the rule?
back: No shooting a firearm, bow or crossbow on or into the developed part of a recreation site: 100 m (109 yd) from any structure, campsite or staging area (99%). Fix: walk 100 m clear first. Never leave guts or scraps there (99%).

front: Rule 38. The slip: a shotgun on the South Thompson flats inside the Kamloops Map C7 band. What is the rule?
back: A No Shooting Area bans firearms; bows are allowed unless restricted. A No Hunting Area bans hunting by any method (99%). Fix: learn the shaded maps for your MU (Management Unit).

front: Rule 39. The slip: hunting the edge of a Mission area park. What is the rule?
back: In Regions 1 and 2, no hunting or shooting within 100 m of any regional district park. Inside towns, the local bylaw decides (99%). Fix: check the park line and the town bylaw before the hunt.

front: Rule 40. The slip: following ducks onto the Vaseux Lake sanctuary. What is the rule?
back: National Wildlife Areas and Migratory Bird Sanctuaries are closed to hunting unless a federal permit or posted notice allows it. Blue loon signs mark the line (99%). Fix: learn the blue loon sign; stop at it.

front: Rule 41. The slip: "It is still light enough" 75 minutes after sunset. What is the rule?
back: Game other than migratory birds: from 1 hour before sunrise to 1 hour after sunset (99%). Fix: look up sunrise and sunset for your spot; set a phone alarm.

front: Rule 42. The slip: shooting ducks at "deer time", 45 minutes before sunrise. What is the rule?
back: Migratory game birds: from 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes after sunset (99%). Fix: on a mixed trip, use the duck clock for everything with feathers on water.

front: Rule 43. The slip: a quail or elk shot in Region 3, where neither has a row (99%). What is the rule?
back: Open seasons are only those in the synopsis. No row for an animal in your MU (Management Unit) means no season (99%). Fix: find the row: species, MU, class, dates. No row, no shot.

front: Rule 44. The slip: a truck spotlight swept over a field "just to look". What is the rule?
back: No hunting with the use or aid of any light or illuminating device (99%). Fix: lights for walking only, never to find, hold or shoot game (90%).

front: Rule 45. The slip: the thermal monocular rides in the pack "only for tracking". What is the rule?
back: No using or possessing infrared optics, thermal scopes and monoculars, on a hunting trip (99%). Fix: leave it at home, not in the truck (95%).

front: Rule 46. The slip: flying the drone the evening before to find the bucks. What is the rule?
back: No operating or possessing a drone on a hunting trip, and no using drone information from less than 6 hours before the trip starts (99%). Fix: leave the drone home on hunting days.

front: Rule 47. The slip: the cell camera on the deer trail in October. What is the rule?
back: No using a wireless camera, one that sends pictures to your phone, for hunting from 1 August to 10 December (99%). Fix: in season, use a camera that only stores to its card (95%).

front: Rule 48. The slip: a phone app call for geese. What is the rule?
back: No recorded or electronic calls except for wolf, coyote, cougar, lynx, bobcat and Schedule C birds. No live decoys or recorded calls for game birds (99%). Fix: mouth and hand calls only (95%).

front: Rule 49. The slip: sitting over last week's gut pile for a bear. What is the rule?
back: No hunting bears over bait or over a dead animal, and no feeding bears, cougars, coyotes or wolves (99%). Fix: hunt bears by glassing and stalking, never over food.

front: Rule 50. The slip: apples out for deer behind the house at Heffley Creek. What is the rule?
back: In Regions 3 and 8, no intentional baiting or feeding of ungulates within 200 m (219 yd) of a dwelling, school yard or playground (99%). Fix: no food out for deer, elk or moose near any home. New this edition (99%).

front: Rule 51. The slip: 3 points plus a brow tine, called a 4 point. What is the rule?
back: A 4 point mule deer buck has at least 4 tines on one antler, not counting the brow tine (99%). Fix: count one side, skip the brow tine, then count again.

front: Rule 52. The slip: counting a short knob to make the fourth point. What is the rule?
back: A tine is at least 2.5 cm (1 in) long and longer than it is wide (99%). Fix: not sure it passes 2.5 cm? It is not a point. No shot.

front: Rule 53. The slip: a forked buck on 2 November. What is the rule?
back: MU (Management Unit) 3-27 and 3-28 mule deer: any buck 1 to 31 October; 4 point bucks only 1 November to 10 December (99%). Fix: read the row for the date, not just the season's end.

front: Rule 54. The slip: cutting the antlers off to pack them out. What is the rule?
back: After an antler or horn restricted season kill, keep the antlers on part of the upper skull, with the licence, until home and butchered, at the meat cutter, or inspected. No altering (99%). Fix: take the skull plate with antlers attached, licence beside it.

front: Rule 55. The slip: a Heffley Creek buck in October, then an Okanagan buck in November. What is the rule?
back: Only 1 mule deer buck a licence year from Regions 3, 4, 5, 6, 7A, 7B and 8 combined, and 3 deer at most in all of BC (99%). Fix: one mule buck between your two interior areas. Mission black tails sit outside it (95%).

front: Rule 56. The slip: "it is a little buck" in a bucks only season. What is the rule?
back: A male fawn with skin covered bumps is antlerless. Antlerless mule deer in Regions 3 and 8 are LEH (Limited Entry Hunting) draw only (99%). Fix: no visible bony antler, no shot, unless you hold the right draw.

front: Rule 57. The slip: a 3 point side read as a fork in poor light. What is the rule?
back: A spike fork bull has no more than 2 tines on one antler, brow palm tines included. A calf never counts (99%). Fix: see both antlers clearly; 2 or fewer on at least one side (90%).

front: Rule 58. The slip: a lone looking sow, cubs out of sight in the brush. What is the rule?
back: No hunting a black bear under 2 years old, or any bear in its company. White and blue (Glacier) colour phases are never legal (99%). Fix: watch a while before the shot, look for small bears.

front: Rule 59. The slip: a deer swimming the lake beside the boat. What is the rule?
back: No hunting, wounding or killing big game while it swims, unless you already wounded it (99%). Fix: let it reach land and leave. No chase with the boat (rule 29).

front: Rule 60. The slip: letting the dog run loose on a wounded deer's trail. What is the rule?
back: Dogs used to hunt deer, elk, moose, sheep, goat and caribou must be on a leash (99%). Fix: tracking dog on a long leash. Off leash only for birds and small game (99%).

front: Rule 61. The slip: a box of lead grouse loads in the vest or the boat. What is the rule?
back: Ducks, geese, coots and snipe: non toxic shot only, and no other shot in your possession in the hunting area (99%). Fix: empty the vest before a duck hunt. Steel, bismuth, tungsten or tin only.

front: Rule 62. The slip: a plug you can thumb out, or a borrowed unplugged gun. What is the rule?
back: Duck gun: 10 gauge or smaller, 3 shells in magazine and chamber together, with a one piece filler you cannot remove without taking the gun apart (99%). Fix: check the plug every season. No slugs (99%).

front: Rule 63. The slip: 8 ducks in the bag, still shooting "for my brother". What is the rule?
back: Once you have the daily limit of a species, you may not keep hunting it that day (99%). Fix: at 8 ducks, unload or switch to geese if they are open (95%).

front: Rule 64. The slip: 8 mallards, then "pintails have their own 4". What is the rule?
back: 8 ducks a day in all. Inside the 8: at most 4 pintails, 4 canvasbacks, 2 goldeneyes, 2 harlequins (99%). Fix: know your ducks on the wing, or pass.

front: Rule 65. The slip: three weekends of unplucked ducks in the fridge. What is the rule?
back: Possession limit is 3 times the daily limit at all times, home included, for every bird not yet preserved (99%). Ducks: 24. Fix: pluck and freeze, or cook, and the bird is preserved (99%).

front: Rule 66. The slip: breasting birds at the marsh and bagging bare meat. What is the rule?
back: A duck or goose keeps one fully feathered wing or the feathered head attached until it is preserved (99%). Fix: breast it if you like, but keep a wing on the piece you carry (85%).

front: Rule 67. The slip: handing your brother 4 ducks at the truck. What is the rule?
back: A duck you shot may not pass to anyone, even for a moment, unless it is labelled or preserved (99%). Fix: a label with your name, contact, date, permit number and signature (99%).

front: Rule 68. The slip: a blind beside grain someone spread for geese. What is the rule?
back: No hunting migratory birds within 400 m (437 yd) of bait until the place has been bait free for 7 days (99%). Fix: ask the farmer what was spread and when. Normal farming spill is not bait (99%).

front: Rule 69. The slip: Mission ducks on 5 October 2026 "because ducks are open". What is the rule?
back: Duck and goose seasons are set by federal District. Heffley Creek is District 3, Mission District 2 (99%). Fix: District 2 ducks open 10 October 2026; District 3 opened 8 September (99%).

front: Rule 70. The slip: cutting the outboard and shooting as you drift into the flock. What is the rule?
back: No hunting migratory birds from or using a moving boat with a motor or sail. Still gliding after the motor is cut counts as moving (99%). Fix: wait until the boat is fully stopped, or hunt from a blind or the kayak.

front: Rule 71. The slip: gutting first, tagging at the truck. What is the rule?
back: After a big game kill, cancel the species licence at once, before handling the animal (99%). Fix: knife stays sheathed until the licence is cancelled.

front: Rule 72. The slip: skinning the tail off, or cutting away the testicles, in the field. What is the rule?
back: A deer carcass you carry keeps the unskinned tail and the evidence of sex naturally attached (99%). Fix: leave both on the hind quarter you keep with you (90%).

front: Rule 73. The slip: butchering at a friend's cabin on the way home. What is the rule?
back: Evidence of species and sex may come off only at home once butchered and stored, at a meat cutter or cold storage plant, or after a compulsory inspection (99%). Fix: keep it whole, evidence on, until your own freezer.

front: Rule 74. The slip: breasting grouse at the truck and bagging only meat. What is the rule?
back: Grouse, quail and other upland birds keep one feathered wing attached while you possess or carry them. A bearded only season turkey keeps the beard (99%). Fix: one wing stays on every bird until home and butchered.

front: Rule 75. The slip: quartering a deer and leaving the neck and ribs. What is the rule?
back: Take the edible portions to your home, a meat cutter or cold storage: big game neck, ribs, all four quarters and loins; birds both breasts (99%). Fix: plan the pack out before the shot. Black bear meat counts too (99%).

front: Rule 76. The slip: "No blood, must have missed," and walking away. What is the rule?
back: Wound or kill game and you must make every reasonable effort to find it, finish it, retrieve it and count it in your bag (99%). Fix: mark the spot, search properly. Ducks: have a dog, waders or boat ready (99%).

front: Rule 77. The slip: no moose, so no report. What is the rule?
back: Everyone who buys an elk, moose or caribou licence files the Mandatory Hunter Report by 31 March, hunt or no hunt (99%). Fix: file in WILD (Wildlife Information and Licensing Data) the week after the season (Tip).

front: Rule 78. The slip: loading the deer your truck hit. What is the rule?
back: You may not possess or transport big game killed by accident or collision. Report any accidental kill to an officer promptly (99%). Fix: call RAPP (Report All Poachers and Polluters), 1 877 952 7277, and leave it (99%).

front: Rule 79. The slip: hiding it, or tagging it with someone else's licence. What is the rule?
back: Shot the wrong animal? Cancel your species licence at once, write in ink on it that you intend to self report, then call RAPP (99%). Fix: cancel, mark in ink, call. Field dress it so the meat keeps (99%).

front: Rule 80. The slip: driving past with an empty truck. What is the rule?
back: All hunters, with or without game, must stop and report at a temporary check station run by an officer (99%). Fix: pull in every time; have licences and ID ready.

front: Rule 81. The slip: venison swapped for a case of beer or a hand with the roof. What is the rule?
back: No selling, trading or bartering wildlife meat for anything of value, and no offering to (99%). Fix: give it, nothing back. A true gift is not trafficking (90%).

front: Rule 82. The slip: selling a few plucked geese to a co worker. What is the rule?
back: No buying or selling migratory birds, their eggs or nests (99%). Fix: give them away, labelled (rule 67), or keep them.

front: Rule 83. The slip: driving your brother's deer home with no paper. What is the rule?
back: To possess or transport meat or parts of an animal someone else killed, carry a Record of Receipt (99%). Fix: write the receipt the moment the meat changes hands; photograph it (Tip).

front: Rule 84. The slip: all four quarters split up, no piece keeps the tail. What is the rule?
back: Your piece of a partner's animal may skip the tail and evidence of sex only if: going to their home, a meat cutter, cold storage or an inspector; with a Record of Receipt; and they keep a piece with the parts attached (99%). Fix: the hunter carries the piece with tail and evidence.

front: Rule 85. The slip: giving 10 unpreserved ducks to someone who already holds 20. What is the rule?
back: Once your friend accepts your ducks, they count toward his possession limit (99%). Fix: ask what they already hold; label every gift (rule 67).

front: Rule 86. The slip: throwing out the cancelled tag in January with half the deer still in the freezer. What is the rule?
back: Keep every document an animal was taken under until the animal has been eaten (99%). Fix: tape the cancelled licence inside the freezer lid (Tip).

front: Rule 87. The slip: dropping the deer off and leaving the tag at camp. What is the rule?
back: At a meat cutter or taxidermist, have your hunting licence and cancelled species licence, plus any LEH (Limited Entry Hunting) authorization or inspection sheet that applies (99%). Fix: the licence goes into the shop with the meat (Tip).

front: Rule 88. The slip: taking a wounded duck home alive, or "rescuing" a fawn. What is the rule?
back: No capturing, possessing or keeping live wildlife without a permit (99%). Fix: finish a wounded bird at once (95%). Leave fawns where they are (Tip).

front: Rule 89. The slip: a whole Alberta deer, head on, in the truck bed. What is the rule?
back: From a deer, elk, moose or caribou killed outside BC, bring in only the meat of quarters, loins, neck and ribs, and a hide, antlers and skull plate cleaned of all tissue (99%). Fix: bone out and clean the skull plate before the BC border.

front: Rule 90. The slip: bagging the whole gut pile to sort at home. What is the rule?
back: No possessing or trafficking bear galls; leave the gall bladder at the kill, or dispose of the gut pile with it within 48 hours. Never sell or trade bear paws (99%). Fix: gall bladder out and left at the kill site.

front: Rule 91. The slip: the Harvest Report sits in one partner's truck. What is the rule?
back: On a shared LEH (Limited Entry Hunting) authorization, carry the Harvest Report section while hunting, fill it in at the kill, and tell every hunter in the group at once (99%). Fix: whoever hunts carries it; text the group the moment an animal is down (Tip).

front: Rule 92. The slip: taking a co worker out "for gas money and a cut of the meat". What is the rule?
back: Helping someone hunt for pay or a promised reward is guiding, and needs a guide licence. Using an unlicensed guide can make you a party to the offence (99%). Fix: help for free, or not at all. Free help for your brother is not guiding (90%).

front: Rule 93. The slip: charging hunters to boat them across the lake. What is the rule?
back: Carrying hunters to, from or between hunting spots for money or other pay makes you a transporter, and needs a transport or guide outfitter licence (99%). Fix: ferry friends for free, never for a fee (90%).

front: Rule 94. The slip: letting a 9 year old take a grouse "with help". What is the rule?
back: No one under 10 may hunt. A person who causes or allows a child under 10 to hunt commits an offence (99%). Fix: under 10, they watch and learn; they do not shoot game.

front: Rule 95. The slip: the youth shoots a buck, then you shoot one too, over your limit. What is the rule?
back: A youth hunter, 10 to under 18, is always accompanied and closely supervised by a qualified adult. Game taken on a youth or initiation licence counts in the supervisor's bag (99%). Fix: count the youth's deer as yours before you shoot.

front: Rule 96. The slip: a first year hunter supervising a nephew. What is the rule?
back: A supervising hunter needs an FWID (Fish and Wildlife ID) with residency and hunting credentials, a hunting licence in at least 3 earlier licence years, no firearms prohibition, and supervises at most two (99%). Fix: check the list before you offer. Your first seasons: you cannot supervise (95%).

front: Rule 97. The slip: signing once for the whole weekend. What is the rule?
back: An initiation licence hunter, 18 or older and never licensed, is accompanied at all times. The supervisor signs a form before each day's hunt (99%). Fix: a fresh signed form every morning.

front: Rule 98. The slip: "supervising" a youth on the next ridge by radio. What is the rule?
back: To accompany is to stay in the person's company, able to see them without binoculars and to talk without a radio or amplifier (99%). Fix: stay close enough to talk in a normal voice.

front: Rule 99. The slip: your first year duck permit, and you take two nephews. What is the rule?
back: A minor on the free federal permit hunts only beside an adult who holds a permit now and held one in an earlier year. One adult, two minors at most (99%). Fix: you qualify from your second permit year on (95%).

front: Rule 100. The slip: setting up in front of another group's decoys, or walking through their stalk on purpose. What is the rule?
back: No interfering with or obstructing a person licensed to hunt, guide or trap while they do it lawfully (99%). Fix: first there keeps the spot; move on (Tip).
